messages.content: Spouse confirmed we can do Friday April 4 through Tuesday April 8. Can you do one last fare and hotel check before I buy? I still want after-school departure, not a late arrival, and Tuesday after lunch. I am willing to pay some extra for DCA and a refundable hotel if the cheaper version is only a little cheaper.

Best pairing still looks like the convenient one. Option A: American Main Cabin ATL-DCA nonstop Friday about 5:48 p.m.-7:32 p.m.; return Tuesday about 1:20 p.m.-3:17 p.m.; around $384 per person. Residence Inn DC Downtown/Convention Center refundable rate around $269/night before taxes, breakfast shown, easy Metro access. Option B: IAD or BWI nonstops price closer to $310-$325 per person, but arrival/transfer is later and more work with a child. Option C: same Residence Inn prepaid saves only about $80-$100 total before tax. My recommendation is A with the refundable hotel unless the final checkout total jumps.
Is there any catch with American versus the Delta flight we compared before? I do not want to land later just for the carrier.

No major catch if you book regular Main Cabin rather than Basic Economy. The comparable Delta nonstop is still acceptable, but it departs later and lands closer to 8:15 p.m., and it is showing slightly higher. American is the better fit for this trip because it gets you into DCA earlier and keeps the Tuesday return after lunch. Seat map caveat: American is showing one three-seat block now, but you should pause if that disappears at checkout.
For the hotel, is prepaid worth considering since the dates are fixed?

I would keep the refundable rate. The prepaid savings are modest compared with the whole trip, and spring-break plans can still get disrupted by illness, weather, or flight changes. The refundable rate appears cancelable until a few days before arrival; verify the exact deadline on the payment page. Breakfast is listed with the Residence Inn rate, but I would also verify that the room type covers three people.
What if we use IAD or BWI and put the savings toward the hotel?

The numbers do not quite justify it. IAD saves roughly $175-$210 total on airfare right now, and BWI is a little more, but both add longer ground transfer and a later/easier-to-fumble arrival. You might save another $100-$180 by staying in Arlington or near an outer Metro stop, but then breakfast, room layout, or museum access becomes less clean. I would only switch away from DCA if the total trip savings clears about $500 and the flight times stay good.
Okay, book path should be American into DCA and the refundable Residence Inn. If the row of three is gone, I want to stop before purchasing.

Good. Booking order: buy the American Main Cabin flights first only if a three-seat block is still available; currently 18 A-C is showing. Then book the Residence Inn refundable rate for April 4-8. Use the room with either two beds or a king plus sofa bed, not a single-king room without a defined third sleeping space.
Please give me the booking note and the final things to verify on the checkout screens.

Booking note: Family DC spring-break trip for three, April 4-8. Book American Main Cabin ATL-DCA nonstop Friday after school, about 5:48 p.m. departure and 7:32 p.m. arrival, with DCA-ATL Tuesday after lunch, about 1:20 p.m. departure. Book Residence Inn Washington, DC Downtown/Convention Center, refundable rate, April 4-8, room for three, breakfast listed, near Metro. Verify before purchase: legal names and birthdates, final fare total, Main Cabin not Basic Economy, seat block together, baggage rules, change/cancellation terms, hotel room occupancy for three, bed/sofa-bed setup, breakfast inclusion on the payment page, cancellation deadline, taxes, and any destination or amenity fee.

messages.content: American just emailed that the Friday ATL-DCA flight moved earlier, from 5:48 to 5:17. School pickup is 2:35 in Decatur. We will have carry-ons only. Is that still workable, or should I look at a later nonstop?

It is workable but tighter. If you leave school by about 2:50, you should aim to be at ATL around 3:45-4:00, which is okay for a 5:17 domestic departure with carry-ons and seats already selected. I would not like it with a checked bag. The later nonstops I see into IAD or BWI add a longer transfer and get you to the hotel much later, so I would keep DCA unless school pickup slips.
We can pack the car before pickup and go straight to the airport. Do I need to do anything about the seats after the schedule change?

Yes, open the reservation and confirm the seat assignments survived the schedule change. If 18 A-C or another three-seat block is still assigned, no action needed. If the airline scattered you, use the schedule-change notice to request a no-fee reseat or call before departure day.
What is the latest we should leave Decatur before this gets stressful?

I would set 2:50 as the target and 3:05 as the hard cutoff. After 3:05, traffic plus security starts to erase the cushion. Check in online the day before, keep bags light, and use the domestic terminal security line that looks shortest when you arrive.
Can you also check the hotel basics? We may want to drop bags Tuesday after checkout, and I want to know if breakfast works for museum mornings.

The Residence Inn listing shows luggage storage/front-desk assistance, but call to confirm because bag storage can be space-dependent. Breakfast hours are typically early enough for museum days, often around 6:30 or 7:00 start, but confirm the weekend and spring-break hours directly with the hotel.
So final recommendation is not to switch?

Correct: keep the DCA flight if you can leave school promptly, stay carry-on only, and confirm the seats are still together. Switch only if pickup will be after 3:05 or if you unexpectedly need to check a bag. Before departure, call the hotel to confirm luggage storage after checkout and exact breakfast hours for Saturday through Tuesday.

messages.content: New work trip: I need to start planning Raleigh-Durham/Cary for a client rollout. Meetings are Tuesday May 6 through Friday May 9, so I think I should fly in Monday evening May 5. The client has not confirmed the exact Cary office address or whether Friday wraps before noon.

Two things drive the plan: the exact office location and the Friday end time. For now I would build around ATL-RDU nonstops, arriving Monday early enough to review materials, and hold off on booking the return until the Friday agenda is clearer. Hotel-wise, I would stay in Cary/Weston or the Cary-RTP edge rather than downtown Raleigh unless the address points there. Are you renting a car, and do you have a nightly cap?

No rental car. Rideshare only. I would like to stay under $220 before taxes if possible, but I can justify more if it keeps the week easier. Solid reviews, roughly 4 or better, breakfast helps, and I need dinner options nearby.

Good shortlist pending the address: Homewood Suites Raleigh-Cary I-40/Weston area, usually strong guest reviews, breakfast included, suite layout, nearby restaurants; Hampton Inn & Suites Raleigh/Cary I-40 area, breakfast included and often cheaper but simpler; Hilton Garden Inn Raleigh-Cary near Crossroads, good dinner access and an on-site restaurant, but breakfast may be paid; Courtyard Raleigh Cary/Crossroads, strong location for restaurants but no free breakfast. I would keep Homewood or Hampton as the lead if the office is near Weston Parkway.
If it turns out to be near Weston Parkway, would Crossroads be annoying?

A little. Crossroads is fine by car, but with rideshares during workday traffic it can turn a 10-minute ride into 20-plus minutes. If the office is near Weston Parkway, Harrison Avenue, or the Cary-RTP side, Homewood/Hampton in that corridor should be lower-friction. Crossroads is better only if the office is south Cary or if restaurant choice beats commute.
Can you give me a couple flight pairs? I prefer nonstop, and I do not want a late Monday arrival if I need to prep.

Flight pair A, safest return: Monday ATL-RDU nonstop around 6:25 p.m.-7:48 p.m.; Friday RDU-ATL around 5:55 p.m.-7:20 p.m. Good if Friday may run past noon. Pair B, earlier return: same Monday outbound, Friday around 2:35 p.m.-4:05 p.m.; only safe if the wrap-up ends by noon. Pair C, possible budget check: Southwest nonstop around 5:30 p.m. Monday and mid/late afternoon Friday, but no assigned seats. I would not add a connection on this short route unless the price difference is unusually large.
The client says Friday might end at 11:30, but they are not ready to promise that. Let's not gamble on the 2:35 return yet.

Then use the 5:55-ish Friday return as the planning lead. It protects you if the wrap-up slips, and RDU is close enough that the later return is inconvenient but not punishing. If they later confirm an 11:30 end, you can reprice the 2:35 option before ticketing.
What should I ask the coordinator before I book?

Ask for the exact office address, visitor entrance or rideshare drop-off point, Friday agenda end time, whether there is a preferred hotel or negotiated rate, and whether any evening team dinner is planned. Also ask if they expect you onsite early Tuesday, because that affects whether the Monday 6:25 arrival gives enough prep time.
Can you give me a booking summary with what is still not confirmed?

Planning summary: solo ATL-RDU work trip for the Cary rollout, travel Monday May 5 after work and return Friday May 9. Flight lead is nonstop ATL-RDU around 6:25 p.m. Monday, with a Friday 5:55-ish RDU-ATL return until the wrap-up time is confirmed. Hotel lead should be Cary/Weston or Cary-RTP, preferably Homewood or Hampton if the office is near Weston Parkway, with breakfast and nearby dinner options verified. Still missing: exact office address, Friday end time, hotel block or negotiated rate, final nightly rates/taxes, cancellation deadline, breakfast details, and final seat availability after ticketing.
